subject: Performance SLO qualification — latency & cost levers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification — latency & cost levers

Alex — thanks for taking the time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to align on SLOs and the cost/performance levers we'll use to hit them.

Call recap (high level):
- Product goal: real-time clinical triage suggestions in the mobile app
- Traffic: bursty daytime traffic, peak ~120 req/s, baseline ~30 req/s (you confirmed)
- Target SLOs you gave on the call: P99 latency ~200ms (end-to-end), sustained throughput ~120 req/s, concurrency target ~8 streams, streaming of partial output required for UI responsiveness

Key constraints and asks from Redwood:
- Sample payloads and token distributions (short clinical notes, avg 120 tokens)
- Traffic profile (10s/1m/5m windows) — helps sizing and warm-up
- Any regulatory notes (you mentioned HIPAA coverage)

Preliminary cost/performance levers we discussed (we'll validate in the tech deep-dive):
1) Continuous batching: short batch windows (10–20ms) to improve GPU throughput while keeping tail latency tight; we can tune the max batching delay per route.
2) KV/prefix caching: if you have repeated prefixes (templates, fixed prompts), we can cache KV state to reduce compute for subsequent tokens — often yields big P99 wins for chat-like flows.
3) Quantization profiles & model variants: offer quantized 13B (int8/8-bit) with fallback to smaller 7B quantized model for extreme tail/backpressure; we’ll validate quality with your eval set.
4) Streaming configuration: chunking and token-group flush (e.g., flush every 4 tokens or X ms) to deliver first bytes quickly while upstreaming batch efficiency.
5) Autoscaling + warm pools: reserved warm capacity to meet P99 under burst; fallback policies to route to lower-cost regions/models if capacity constrained.

Action items / next steps:
- I attached an SLO_matrix.xlsx to capture exact target numbers and anticipated traffic buckets (please review)
- Can you send the traffic CSV and 1–2 sample payloads? (Sam or Alex)
- Technical deep-dive to validate batching/caching/quantization options — propose Tue 8/11 10am PT (I'll send a calendar invite)

Questions for you before the deep-dive:
- Is there a hard first-byte target for streaming (e.g., <80ms)?
- Any hard constraints on model quantization (do you require FP32 for clinical safety evaluation?)
- Target cost per 1k tokens or cost goal we should optimize toward?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and a short pre-read that maps the levers above to rough cost impact.

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — latency & cost levers

Thanks Rishi — good summary. Sam and I reviewed and a few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive: 

- Streaming: our mobile UX needs first-byte as fast as possible for perceived latency. We'd like first byte ideally <80ms and P50 first byte ~50–70ms. Full completion can be slower but P99 end-to-end should stay under ~250ms.
- Traffic: attaching the traffic profile CSV (orchid_traffic_profile.csv) — it includes 24h sample and 1-week peak windows.
- Quantization: clinical team is open to quantized models for inference as long as we can validate output parity on our eval set. We will need to run offline checks.
- Compliance: HIPAA is required — please include SOC2 and data residency notes in the pre-read.

One more ask: can Redwood support SSE-based streaming for partial tokens (not just websocket)? Our client infra prefers SSE to reduce complexity.

Happy to do Tue 8/11 10am PT. Sam will join the tech deep-dive and pass along additional sample prompts.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, Orchid Health
alex.chen@orchidhealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — latency & cost levers

Alex — perfect, thanks for the file and the streaming target. Quick replies inline + agenda for the tech deep-dive: 

Inline: 
- First-byte target: we can design for <80ms first byte by combining warm pools, small initial KV cache checks, and eager flush policy in the streaming layer.
- SSE streaming: yes, Redwood supports SSE in addition to WebSocket; we'll demo token chunking and flush tuning in the deep-dive.
- Quantization validation: we'll run your eval set against both FP32 baseline and our quantized 13B (GPTQ int8 / optional 4-bit profile) and produce a delta report prior to any rollout.
- Compliance: Marissa will attach SOC2 and our data residency options in the pre-read.

Proposed preliminary config to test in the deep-dive (we'll validate with your traffic):
- Batch window: 10ms target, max batching delay 20ms (tunable)
- Continuous batching algo: latency-aware batching with per-route max latency cap
- Caching: prefix/KV caching enabled for prompts with >30% reuse; expect 40–70% token compute savings on chat flows
- Quantization profiles:
  • Performance profile: 13B int8 (GPTQ) — primary
  • Cost-saver profile: 13B 4-bit (experimental) or 7B int8 fallback for heavy tail
- Streaming: flush every 3–5 tokens or after 30ms (whichever comes first) to balance first-byte latency and throughput
- Warm pools: keep a small reserved pool sized for ~30% of peak to hit P99 during spikes

Next steps: 
1) We'll send a calendar invite for Tue 8/11 10am PT with a short agenda (deep-dive + quantization validation plan).
2) Priyom (copied) will bring a perf run template and initial cost sensitivity numbers for the configurations above.
3) Please confirm if we should include a security contact on the call for the compliance portion.

If that looks good I’ll attach a short pre-read (SOC2, SLO_matrix with configurable fields, and a rough cost delta table) and a link to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Rishi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
